theory.intro: Going down a list of powers divides by the base each time, and dividing a power by itself gives $1$. Both patterns point to the same result: any non-zero base to the power of $0$ is $1$.
facts: Stepping down the indices divides by the base each time: $2^{3}=8$, $2^{2}=4$, $2^{1}=2$, so $2^{0}=2\div2=1$.
The index law of division gives the same result: $9^{2}\div 9^{2}=9^{2-2}=9^{0}$, and a number divided by itself is $1$.
The index applies only to what it is written against: $(-5)^{0}=1$, but $-5^{0}=-\left(5^{0}\right)=-1$.
A base of $0$ behaves differently: $0^{5}=0$. The zero-index rule requires a nonzero base; in this work, $0^{0}$ is left undefined.
steps: Check what the index is attached to — the whole bracket, or just the number in front of it.
Replace each zero power of a nonzero base by $1$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Continue the pattern $6^{3}=216$, $6^{2}=36$, $6^{1}=6$ to find $6^{0}$.
Explain why the answer is not $0$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Each step down in the index divides by the base $6$.
$6^{2}=216\div6=36$
$6^{1}=36\div6=6$
$6^{0}=6\div6=1$.
The next step divides $6$ by $6$; it does not make the value zero.

workedExamples.question_text: Use $8^{3}\div8^{3}$ to establish the value of $8^{0}$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The division law subtracts the indices:
$8^{3}\div8^{3}=8^{3-3}=8^{0}$.
Also, $8^{3}=512$ and $512\div512=1$.
Both expressions describe the same division, so $8^{0}=1$.
The base is nonzero, so dividing by this power is allowed.

(a) The whole bracket is the nonzero base, so $(-7)^{0}=1$.
(b) The index is attached only to $7$. The minus sign stays outside.
$-7^{0}=-\left(7^{0}\right)=-1$.
(c) The base $\frac{1}{5}$ is nonzero, so $\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^{0}=1$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Evaluate $0^{4}$.
(b) Explain why the zero-index rule cannot be used to give $0^{0}$ a value.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $0^{4}=0\times0\times0\times0=0$.
This is a zero base with a positive index.
(b) The rule $a^{0}=1$ requires a nonzero base, so it does not apply to $0^{0}$.
The rule $0^{n}=0$ requires a positive whole-number index, so it does not apply either.
The division argument would require $0\div0$, which is not allowed. In this work, $0^{0}$ is left undefined.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Evaluate $13\times6^{0}+5^{0}$.
(b) Arrange $-8^{0}$, $0^{8}$ and $(-8)^{0}$ in ascending order.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Evaluate each zero power before the remaining operations.
$13\times6^{0}+5^{0}=13\times1+1=14$.
(b) $-8^{0}=-1$, $0^{8}=0$ and $(-8)^{0}=1$.
Since $-1<0<1$, the ascending order is $-8^{0},\ 0^{8},\ (-8)^{0}$.

(a) $23^{8}$ is nonzero, so $\left(23^{8}\right)^{0}=1$. There is no need to work out $23^{8}$.
(b) First replace the zero powers of nonzero bases by $1$.
$\left(4^{0}\right)^{6}-(-8)^{0}+0^{2}$
$=1^{6}-1+0$
$=1-1+0$
$=0$.

foundation.question_text: Use the index law of division to write $9^{2}\div 9^{2}$ as a power of $9$, then use the fact that a number divided by itself is $1$ to state the value of $9^{0}$.

development.solution_text:
$\left(91^{23}\right)^{0}$
$=1$
The whole bracket is the base and $91^{23}$ is nonzero, so the zero-index rule applies.

mastery.question_text:
A student says $5^{0}=0$ because "there are no fives left to multiply".
Use the pattern of descending powers of $5$ to explain the error.
mastery.solution_text:
$5^{3}=125$
$5^{2}=125\div5=25$
$5^{1}=25\div5=5$
$5^{0}=5\div5=1$
Each step down divides by $5$, it does not remove the value altogether. The pattern lands on $1$, not $0$.

mastery.question_text: Explain why $0^{0}$ is undefined, using the two patterns $a^{0}=1$ and $0^{n}=0$.
mastery.solution_text:
The rule $a^{0}=1$ requires a nonzero base, so it does not give a value for $0^{0}$.
The rule $0^{n}=0$ requires a positive whole-number index, so it does not give a value for $0^{0}$ either.
The division argument also breaks down: it would require $0\div0$, and division by $0$ is not allowed.
In this work, $0^{0}$ is left undefined.
